title: SSH private keys
whyItMatters: Private keys in this folder can grant access to servers and Git hosts without a password. They must be rotated if the machine changes hands.
source: OpenSSH user key location: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_keymanagement (user keys under ~/.ssh)
notes: Metadata only; key material is never opened. Known_hosts and config files in the same folder are included in the count.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy the keys you still need to the machine you are moving to, or make new keys there, before deleting anything here.
cleanup.signOut: Remove the public key from every server and Git host that trusts it, and change anything those keys protected.
steps: Make a list of the servers and hosts that trust these keys.
Remove the public key from each one and add a new key where you still need access.
Delete the folder named in the plan.
cleanup.risk: Deletes the private keys on this PC for good. Anything still trusting those keys stays reachable until you remove the public key from it.
cleanup.source: Microsoft Learn, Key Management for OpenSSH on Windows: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_keymanagement
